instruction.instruction:
Escalate the conversation to a human agent when you cannot provide adequate assistance, when other tools fail or return errors, or when the customer's request requires human intervention. and also when:
 1. The customer explicitly requests to speak to a human agent or advisor
  2. The customer is frustrated or distressed
  3. The issue is too complex to resolve with available tools
  4. You have attempted to resolve the issue and cannot do so
When escalating to a human agent, always populate the input fields as follows:
- topicCategory: choose the closest match to the primary subject of the customer's
  enquiry (e.g. "mortgage" if they were asking about their mortgage balance or
  overpayments, "fraud_security" if they reported suspicious activity).
- escalationReason: set to "customer_requested" if the customer explicitly asked for
  a human. Set to "complaint" if they expressed dissatisfaction or used complaint
  language. Set to "complex_request" if the issue is beyond your available tools.
  Set to "technical_issue" if a tool returned repeated errors.
- customerIntent: a brief phrase, e.g. "wants to discuss mortgage overpayment options"
  or "reporting suspected card fraud".
- conversationSummary: one or two sentences summarising what was discussed and what
  the customer needs, so the human agent does not have to ask the customer to repeat
  themselves.
examples:
Good example - Tool errors:
<message>
I'm having trouble accessing the information you need right now. Would you like me to connect you with a human agent who can help you further?
</message>

Good example - Frustrated customer:
<message>
I understand your frustration with this issue. Would you like me to connect you with a human agent who can help you further?
</message>

Bad example (avoid this):
<message>
I'm unable to help with this. Let me escalate you to a human agent.
</message>
Good Example - Customer ask:
Good Example - AI Agent ask:

topicCategory.description: The primary banking topic the customer was enquiring about

escalationReason.description: Why ARIA is escalating to a human agent

instruction.instruction:
Use when the customer wants to apply for a new mortgage or start a mortgage application.
   Before using it, ask once: "Do you have your application open on screen? If so, there's a
   6-digit code under 'Get help by phone' - could you read it to me?" If they read one, include
   it as screenCode (digits only). If they don't have it open, use the tool without it.
   Do not use for questions about an existing mortgage.

toolConfigurations.title: aws_service__qconnect_Retrieve
toolConfigurations.description: Searches the knowledge base to return relevant knowledge article excerpts.

instruction.instruction:
Semantic search over the knowledge base. It takes any natural-language query and returns excerpts, one result per excerpt, each shaped {"sourceId":"s3://<bucket>/<kbId>/<contentId>","contentText":"…","referenceType":"KNOWLEDGE_BASE","associationId":"…"}. When a long general excerpt does not state what the case at hand needs, run it again with a narrower query before answering. When results are empty, say you don't have that specific information; never fill the gap from general knowledge. A non-empty errors array means part of the search failed: answer from the results that did come back, and when they do not cover the question say that the specific information did not come back.

CITING. A <message> that states information drawn from a result carries a citation without being asked: one <sourceId> per result it draws on, copied verbatim (s3://<bucket>/<kbId>/<contentId>), never shortened or rebuilt. A result the message does not use is not cited, however many came back, so every source link the reader opens backs a line they just read. A <message> that states no retrieved content carries no citation. When a short progress line previews what a later message states in full, the citation goes once, on the message that states it; the progress line stays plain.

THE WRAPPER. A cited <message> holds one <message_part>: the whole body inside <text>, then <sources>, then the closing tags, all on one line: <message><message_part><text>…the whole body…</text><sources><sourceId>…</sourceId></sources></message_part></message>. A reply that mixes results from other tools with retrieved content still uses one part, the <sources> covering the retrieved portion. Nothing else about the message changes: the same body an uncited <message> would carry, with the wrapper around it. Whatever the body ends with, a trailing space included, ends before </text>; nothing sits between </text> and <sources>. Only text inside a <message> reaches the reader: a <message_part> outside one is dropped whole. After the last </sourceId> the next characters are always </sources></message_part></message>; a <sources> block left open is never finalized, and the message is lost from the conversation history.

toolConfigurations.title: aws_service__qconnect_Retrieve
toolConfigurations.description: Searches the knowledge base to return relevant knowledge article excerpts.

instruction.instruction:
Search the knowledge base using semantic search to find relevant information.

When summarizing retrieve tool results, you must include source citations in the format shown in good examples below.
MUST ensure every message_part has sources. You can include preamble text like 'Here's what I found' but combine it with sourced content in the same message_part.
MUST include source citations for ALL information from retrieve results.
Additional messages which do not need citations can be included in separate message blocks.
If retrieve returns no results or empty results, acknowledge that you don't have that specific information available. Do not make assumptions or provide information from general knowledge.
examples:
Good example - multiple message parts with sources.
<message>
  <message_part>
    <text>This is the first part of the answer.</text>
    <sources>
      <sourceId>sampleSourceId_1</sourceId>
      <sourceId>sampleSourceId_2</sourceId>
    </sources>
  </message_part>
  <message_part>
    <text>This is the second part with different sources.</text>
    <sources>
      <sourceId>sampleSourceId_3</sourceId>
    </sources>
  </message_part>
</message>

Good example - single message part with source
 <message>
   <message_part>
     <text>I found information about your warranty. It covers parts replacement for any manufacturing defects during the first year.</text>
     <sources>
       <sourceId>warranty_policy_2024</sourceId>
     </sources>
   </message_part>
 </message>

Bad example - message parts without sources (avoid this):
 <message>
   <message_part>
     <text>Here's what I found about your warranty:</text>
   </message_part>
   <message_part>
     <text>It covers parts replacement.</text>
     <sources>
       <sourceId>warranty_policy_2024</sourceId>
     </sources>
   </message_part>
 </message>

Bad example - Text outside message parts after citations (avoid this):
 <message>
   <message_part>
     <text>Your warranty covers parts replacement for manufacturing defects.</text>
     <sources>
       <sourceId>warranty_policy_2024</sourceId>
     </sources>
   </message_part>
   Let me know if you need anything else.
 </message>

Bad example - Providing information from retrieve results without citations (avoid this):
 <message>
 We offer extended warranty coverage for eligible products beyond the manufacturer's warranty period.
 </message>

Good example - some messages with citations and some without:
<message>
  <message_part>
    <text>Based on our return policy, you can return most items within 30 days of purchase for a full refund. Items must be in original condition with receipt or proof of purchase.</text>
    <sources>
      <sourceId>return_policy_2024</sourceId>
      <sourceId>customer_handbook_3_2</sourceId>
    </sources>
  </message_part>
</message>

<message>
I'm still looking up the specific warranty coverage details for electronics. I'll have that information for you shortly.
</message>

Example for no results:
<message>
I don't have specific information about that topic available.
</message>

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__queue-status___get_queue_status
toolConfigurations.description: Live status of the human colleague queue that handles a topic: whether it is open right now (is_open_now — the ONLY authority on queue openness), today's hours, whether agents are signed in (agents_staffed / agents_available), how many callers are waiting (contacts_in_queue) and a rough estimated_wait_minutes (null when nobody is signed in — say the team is unavailable instead of a number). instruction.instruction:
Escalate the conversation to a human agent when you cannot provide adequate assistance, when other tools fail or return errors, or when the customer's request requires human intervention. and also when:
 1. The customer explicitly requests to speak to a human agent or advisor
  2. The customer is frustrated or distressed
  3. The issue is too complex to resolve with available tools
  4. You have attempted to resolve the issue and cannot do so
When escalating to a human agent, always populate the input fields as follows:
- topicCategory: choose the closest match to the primary subject of the customer's
  enquiry (e.g. "mortgage" if they were asking about their mortgage balance or
  overpayments, "fraud_security" if they reported suspicious activity).
- escalationReason: set to "customer_requested" if the customer explicitly asked for
  a human. Set to "complaint" if they expressed dissatisfaction or used complaint
  language. Set to "complex_request" if the issue is beyond your available tools.
  Set to "technical_issue" if a tool returned repeated errors.
- customerIntent: a brief phrase, e.g. "wants to discuss mortgage overpayment options"
  or "reporting suspected card fraud".
- conversationSummary: one or two sentences summarising what was discussed and what
  the customer needs, so the human agent does not have to ask the customer to repeat
  themselves.
examples:
Good example - Tool errors:
<message>
I'm having trouble accessing the information you need right now. Would you like me to connect you with a human agent who can help you further?
</message>

Good example - Frustrated customer:
<message>
I understand your frustration with this issue. Would you like me to connect you with a human agent who can help you further?
</message>

Bad example (avoid this):
<message>
I'm unable to help with this. Let me escalate you to a human agent.
</message>

conversationSummary.description: One or two sentence summary of the conversation for the human agent to read when they pick up

customerIntent.description: Brief phrase describing what the customer was trying to accomplish

topicCategory.description: The primary banking topic the customer was enquiring about

escalationReason.description: Why ARIA is escalating to a human agent

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__branch-info___find_branches
toolConfigurations.description: Search Nationwide Building Society and Virgin Money branches by town, area, postcode or outcode. Optionally filter by brand and by a required service (e.g. 'mortgage advice', 'counter cash', 'business banking'). Returns location, phone, today's opening hours, is_open_now (the ONLY authority on whether the branch is open right now — never work it out yourself) and the services available at each matching branch. Use get_branch_details for full opening times.

service.description: Only return branches offering this service. Canonical values: counter cash, cash deposit, cheque deposit, mortgage advice, savings advice, financial planning, business banking, safe custody. Also accepted: 'atm' or 'cash machine' (branches with an ATM) and accessibility terms such as 'wheelchair access' or 'hearing loop'. Map the customer's words to the closest canonical value.

query.description: Town, area, full postcode or outcode, e.g. 'Leeds', 'SW1E 5NH', 'NE3'.

limit.description: Maximum number of branches to return (default 5).

brand.description: Restrict results to one brand. Default: any. Natural forms ('Virgin Money', 'Nationwide Building Society') are also accepted.

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__branch-info___get_branch_details
toolConfigurations.description: Get the full record for one branch by its branch_id (from a find_branches result): complete address, phone, opening times for all seven days, today's hours, is_open_now (the ONLY authority on whether the branch is open right now), every service offered, accessibility features and ATM availability.

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__branch-appointments___book_branch_appointment
toolConfigurations.description: Book a confirmed appointment at a branch for the customer, with the reason for their visit. Only book a date and time that get_appointment_slots returned, and only after the customer confirmed the slot, their name, and the reason. Returns a confirmation message with an appointment reference to read back to the customer. If the slot was just taken, offer another slot.

date.description: Appointment date, format YYYY-MM-DD, within the next 7 days.

reason.description: Why the customer is visiting, short, in their own words — e.g. 'rearrange a mortgage document appointment'. Same reason already captured for the conversation.

contact_phone.description: Optional contact number, only if the customer volunteers one.

branch_id.description: Branch identifier from a find_branches result, e.g. 'NBS-0002'. Never typed from memory.

time.description: Appointment start time, format HH:MM (24-hour), taken from get_appointment_slots.

customer_name.description: The customer's name for the branch diary, as they gave it.

topic_category.description: Optional canonical topic if one fits: branch_services, mortgages, savings, business_banking, bereavement, power_of_attorney, financial_difficulty, fraud_security, complaint, general.

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__branch-appointments___get_appointment_slots
toolConfigurations.description: List bookable appointment slots at one branch for the next 7 days (or a single date). Slots are hourly, within the branch's opening hours, at least 1 hour ahead, and exclude times already booked. Always call this before offering or booking a time — never invent availability. Use the branch_id from a find_branches result.

date.description: Optional single date to check, format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. '2026-07-08'). Omit to get the full 7-day window.

branch_id.description: Branch identifier from a find_branches result, e.g. 'NBS-0002' or 'VM-0001'. Never typed from memory.

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__branch-info___get_current_time
toolConfigurations.description: Get the current date and time in the United Kingdom (Europe/London): day of week, date, 24-hour time, ISO timestamp and timezone. This is your ONLY clock — call it before any time-dependent statement or decision: whether a branch has closed for the day, when it reopens, what day 'tomorrow' is, or which days suit an appointment. Takes no arguments.

toolConfigurations.title: gateway_aria-banking-mcp-gateway-prod-11grjuxyru__queue-status___get_queue_status
toolConfigurations.description: Live status of the human colleague queue that handles a topic: whether it is open right now (is_open_now — the ONLY authority on queue openness), today's hours, whether agents are signed in (agents_staffed / agents_available), how many callers are waiting (contacts_in_queue) and a rough estimated_wait_minutes (null when nobody is signed in — say the team is unavailable instead of a number). Call this BEFORE transferring a customer to a human queue so you can set friendly, rounded expectations — 'around five minutes', never raw numbers or promises — or offer the automatic callback / a branch appointment when the team is unavailable. If the topic is not recognised the response lists known_topics — pick the closest and call again. A failed check must never block or delay a transfer.

topic_category.description: The conversation's topic category — the same value you will put on the transfer, e.g. 'mortgages', 'branch_services', 'savings', 'general', 'complaint', 'fraud_security'.
